proposals.before: Chongyi also cited the Winter Office, Jade Workers: "The perforation of the bi is three cun," and the Erya: "When the rim is twice the perforation it is called a bi"; the rim on each side is three cun, and the perforation altogether nine cun—thus the nine-cun bi is clear.
proposals.after: Chongyi also cited the Winter Office, Jade Workers: "The perforation of the bi is three cun," and the Erya: "When the rim is twice the perforation it is called a bi"; the rim on each side is three cun, which together with the perforation makes nine cun in all—thus the nine-cun bi is clear.
proposals.reason: Literal English wrongly collapses rim-plus-hole into “the perforation altogether nine cun,” contradicting the Chinese arithmetic (兩邊肉各三寸，通好共九寸).

proposals.before: Your subjects observe that Jingzong in life was once emperor; offerings continue the ancestral line—having been called Jingzong, he should enter the ancestral temple; if he does not enter the ancestral temple, it is difficult to speak of 'zong.
proposals.after: Your subjects observe that Jingzong in life was once emperor; offerings continue the ancestral line—having been called Jingzong, he should enter the ancestral temple; if he does not enter the ancestral temple, it is difficult to speak of 'zong.'
proposals.reason: Literal English drops the closing quotation mark after zong and truncates the sentence punctuation present in the Chinese sense.

proposals.before: The Rites say: "After the end of wailing, the steward takes a wooden clapper and announces through the palace, saying 'Abandon the old taboo and observe the new.'
proposals.after: The Rites say: "After the end of wailing, the steward takes a wooden clapper and announces through the palace, saying 'Abandon the old taboo and observe the new.'"
proposals.reason: Literal English omits the closing quotation marks that close the embedded and outer quotations.

proposals.before: Old' means the lord of a destroyed temple; when favor is distant and kinship severed, the name need not be tabooed.
proposals.after: 'Old' means the lord of a destroyed temple; when favor is distant and kinship severed, the name need not be tabooed.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English begins with Old' without an opening quotation mark, though it glosses the quoted 故.

decisions.reason: 兩邊肉各三寸，通好共九寸 means each rim is three cun and, together with the perforation (好), totals nine cun. The before wrongly makes the perforation alone nine cun; the after restores the rim-plus-hole arithmetic.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 兩邊肉各三寸，通好共九寸

decisions.reason: The focus unit ends 難以言宗。; the literal opens a quote on 'zong but never closes it. Adding the closing mark after zong fixes a real punctuation defect without changing sense.
Chinese closes the Rites citation with 」 after 舍故而諱新; the literal opens a double quote for that citation and never closes it. The after supplies the missing outer closing quote.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 《禮》云：「卒哭之後，宰執木鐸徇於宮，曰舍故而諱新。」

decisions.reason: 故 is glossed as the quoted Old from the prior Rites line; idiomatic begins Old' with only a closing mark. Restoring the opening quote matches the Chinese lemma and the already-correct literal.
